US Technology Services Trade Figures Show Modest Growth in First Quarter

WASHINGTON, June 20 — The United States technology services sector recorded steady growth in international trade during the first quarter of 2024, according to data released Thursday by the Bureau of Economic Analysis. Exports of technology services, including software development, IT consulting, and cloud computing, reached $64.8 billion, up 2.6% from the previous quarter.

Imports in the sector also increased, rising to $48.1 billion, a gain of 2.0% over the previous period. The trade surplus for US technology services expanded slightly to $16.7 billion, reflecting continued demand for American digital solutions in key overseas markets.

Industry representatives described the figures as indicative of stable demand amid a competitive global environment. “We’re seeing consistent growth across software engineering and cybersecurity services, especially in Western Europe and Southeast Asia,” said Priya Desai, spokesperson for the American Technology Services Association. “This underscores the US’s continued leadership in innovation and digital exports.”

Analysts noted that the gradual rise in both exports and imports reflects ongoing international collaboration and robust technology investment by US firms. “The data suggest that American providers remain attractive partners globally, even as firms increasingly source specialized expertise from abroad,” said Miguel Aranda, senior analyst at Finway Insights.

The figures come as companies such as InfoPulse Solutions and NextGen TechWorks report stronger overseas orders, particularly for cloud migration and enterprise automation services. “We continue to see expansion opportunities in Latin America and the Middle East,” said Emma Liu, Chief Commercial Officer at NextGen TechWorks.

The Bureau’s report also highlighted steady employment in the sector, with technology services jobs holding at just over 5.1 million nationwide. Wages in the industry rose 1.3% from the previous quarter.

No significant disruptions or policy changes were reported during the period. Trade bodies expect moderate growth to continue through the rest of the year, citing persistent demand for digital transformation and enterprise IT modernization worldwide.
